title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'Chirurgie des surfaces conformes' notes, Grothendieck classifies anti-holomorphic involutions (real structures) σ on a complex torus X = C/Π. On the previous pages he sorted them by lattice symmetry (square, hexagonal, generic) into two families, E_a and E'_a. This page has two parts.

(1) Summary: the period τ for each type.
- Type E_a. The lattice Π = Ze0 + Ze1 is rectangular.
  - σ fixes e0 and negates e1.
  - The quadratic form is Q(xe0 + ye1) = x² + a y².
  - Normalizing Q to the standard form sends e0 ↦ 1 and e1 ↦ √a·i, so τ = i√a.
- Type E'_a. The lattice is rhombic (centered rectangular), Π = Zu + Zv.
  - σ fixes u and sends v ↦ u − v.
  - The invariant vector is e0 = u and the anti-invariant vector is e1 = 2v − u, with Q(xe0 + ye1) = x² + a y².
  - The vectors e0 and e1/√a form an orthonormal basis, so u ↦ 1 and v = (e0 + e1)/2 ↦ (1 + i√a)/2.
  - Hence τ = 1/2 + (√a/2) i.
These are exactly the two classical normal forms of real elliptic curves: Im-axis lattices with τ ∈ iR, and lattices with Re τ = 1/2.

(2) Start of the computation of the group of real points X(R).
- Real points are the x mod Π, with x ∈ Π⊗R, such that σx ≡ x mod Π.
- For E_a, σ(x, y) = (x, −y), so σ(x, y) − (x, y) = (0, −2y). The condition is 2y ∈ Z, i.e. y ∈ {0, 1/2} mod Z.
- So X(R) = (R/Z)e0 ⊔ ((1/2)e1 + (R/Z)e0): two circles, i.e. X(R) ≅ S¹ × Z/2.
- The E'_a case (one component, X(R) ≅ S¹) is presumably treated on the next page, which moves on to a classification of involutions in GL(2) over 2-regular rings.

Purpose: this is a toolkit for classifying the real structures and reflection symmetries of tori arising from regular tilings (square, hexagonal), as part of the 'surgery' of conformal surfaces.
errors: No error on this page itself. The computations of τ and of the two real components for E_a are correct.

Inconsistency with the previous page: there, for the hexagonal case, Grothendieck writes a = Q(2v−u)/Q(u) = √3. With |u| = |v| = 1 and a 60° angle, Q(2v−u) = 4 + 1 − 2 = 3, so a = 3 if a is the ratio of Q-values, as on this page. Taking a = 3 gives τ = (1 + √3 i)/2, the correct hexagonal period. The √3 is the ratio of lengths, not of squared lengths.
Sign slip, harmless: σ(x,y) − (x,y) = (0, −2y), not (0, 2y). The condition 2y ∈ Z is unaffected.

ideas.what: Two types of real structures on a complex torus: rectangular lattice (τ = i√a, two real components) and rhombic lattice (τ = 1/2 + i√a/2, one real component).
ideas.modern_name: Classification of real elliptic curves / anti-holomorphic involutions of complex tori (number of real components, Klein's classification of symmetric Riemann surfaces in genus 1)

ideas.what: Computing X(R) as the fixed points of σ on (Π⊗R)/Π via the condition σx − x ∈ Π.
ideas.modern_name: Real points of a real torus; H¹(Z/2, Π) counts the components

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, correct derivation of the normal forms of real elliptic curves and their real point groups, done as a working tool. It contains nothing beyond the classical theory.
transcription_corrections: The final line should read roughly: 'Donc y = 0 ou 1/2 : les pts de (R/Z)e0 et de (1/2)e1 + (R/Z)e0, donc deux composantes connexes pour X(R)'. The machine rendering '(R/Z)(e1·1/2) + R e0' is garbled.
In the E'_a part, 'on prend une base' is struck out, and the text reads 'on change un peu de base'.
Image check: σ(x,y) = (x, −y) and σ(x,y) − (x,y) is written as (0, 2y) in the manuscript; the sign is the author's own slip.
